message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"12","text":"The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment and closely investigating the actions of each person in the church to determine who is about to sin, so that, once caught by the admonition of the one who presides, that person perhaps may not carry out the sin at all. They should bring back those who desert their posts, so as not to abandon those who come together to listen to the discourses, so that they may be able, by the word of truth, to cleanse away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For whenever they have lain fallow for a long time, they become material for fire. They should also identify those who are ill in the flesh and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that they may appear, and they should provide what is needed according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should take thought for these and similar matters.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι ἔστωσαν ὀφθαλμοί","chosen":"should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment","rationale":"Preserves both the image of the deacons as the bishop’s eyes and the discerning movement expressed by the participle and adverb."},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν","chosen":"closely investigating the actions of each person in the church to determine who is about to sin","rationale":"Treats τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν as the question guiding the deacons’ close investigation."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λειποτάκτας ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν","chosen":"They should bring back those who desert their posts","rationale":"Retains the military image in λειποτάκτας and renders ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν as restoring the deserters."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","chosen":"so as not to abandon those who come together to listen to the discourses","rationale":"Takes the articular infinitive as expressing purpose, its unexpressed subject as the deacons, and τοὺς συνερχομένους as the object of transitive ἐπιλείπειν. The infinitive ἐπακούειν supplies the purpose for which the people come together."},{"source_quote":"τὰς ἑκάστοτε τῇ καρδίᾳ προσπιπτούσας ἀθυμίας ἔκ τε βιωτικῶν συνπτώσεων καὶ ὁμιλιῶν κακῶν λόγῳ ἀληθείας καθαίρεσθαι","chosen":"by the word of truth, to cleanse away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations","rationale":"Preserves the image of discouragements falling upon the heart, the two stated sources of them, and the instrumental force of λόγῳ ἀληθείας."},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","chosen":"For whenever they have lain fallow for a long time, they become material for fire","rationale":"Retains the agricultural image of lying fallow and the subsequent image of becoming something upon which fire works, while leaving the plural subject unresolved."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας μανθανέτωσαν","chosen":"They should also identify those who are ill in the flesh","rationale":"Renders μανθανέτωσαν as ascertaining who is ill while retaining the explicit bodily qualification κατὰ σάρκα."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","chosen":"and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that they may appear","rationale":"Represents the apparent presentation or notification directed toward the unaware multitude without specifying more than ἐπιφαίνωνται itself states."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","issue":"The articular infinitive with τοῦ μή has purpose force, but the syntax permits materially different readings. The main text treats the deacons as the unexpressed subject of transitive ἐπιλείπειν, τοὺς συνερχομένους as its accusative object, and ἐπακούειν as the purpose of their assembling. Alternatively, τοὺς συνερχομένους may be the accusative subject of intransitive ἐπιλείπειν: “so that those who come together to hear the discourses do not fail” or “do not fall away.” If ἐπακούειν is instead construed as complementary to ἐπιλείπειν, the sense is “so that those who come together do not fail or cease to listen to the discourses.” This is an interpretive ambiguity in the supplied Greek, not evidence of textual or OCR corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","issue":"The plural subject of χερσεύσωσιν and γίνονται is not explicit. It may refer to the discouragements, to the people who assemble and hear, or to people understood through the image of land lying fallow. The translation retains the unresolved pronoun “they.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","issue":"The precise force of προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται remain uncertain. The sick may be brought to the multitude’s attention and then appear or present themselves, but the plural subject could instead be members of the previously unaware multitude appearing on the scene. The supplied reading is intelligible enough to translate provisionally and is not being treated as corrupt.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"συνπτώσεων","issue":"The supplied edition has the unassimilated spelling συνπτώσεων. The normalized spelling συμπτώσεων would express the same word and meaning; this is an orthographic feature rather than evidence of OCR corruption.","proposed_reading":"συμπτώσεων","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
